task.title: Stop simultaneous creates on the board failing with a rebuild error
task.description:
When several tasks are created through the board at the same moment, some of the requests fail with `500 cannot refresh projection cache after a concurrent update; run workbook rebuild`. The message sends the person to run a rebuild they do not need: the cache is fine, the create simply lost a race and was not written.

Measured on 2026-11-21 by the review of "Cap how much work the board does at once" (PR #211): with 300 simultaneous creates, 151 to 209 failed this way on a build without the cap, and 0 to 4 with it. None of the failed creates was written (0 of 615 appeared in the task list), and the page does not send a 500 again, so nothing is duplicated; the person's task is just not created and they are told the wrong thing to do.

The cap makes it rare but does not remove it, and a command-line user racing a board or a background sync can presumably hit the same path.

## What is needed

- Find why refreshing the cache after a concurrent update fails rather than retrying against the new state.
- A create or edit that loses this race either succeeds after refreshing, or is refused with an answer the client can safely send again.
- The message never tells a person to run `workbook rebuild` when a rebuild would change nothing.

## Done when

- A test with many simultaneous creates through the web API finishes with every request either written or refused with a retryable answer, and none answered 500.
- The same holds for simultaneous edits to different tasks.
